title: SSP-2 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery
summary: deliver the live folder-centred Project State report and its versioned downstream lookup
content_html:
SSP-2 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery

Status And Purpose

SSP-2 is complete after the accepted SSP-2.0 sanity gate, SSP-2.1 producer and versioned lookup, SSP-2.2 basic report, and SSP-2.3 browser interactions. SSP-2.0 — Project State Sanity Note records the implementation fit and direct-project-folder boundary. SSP-2.1 — Project State Producer Evidence records the producer, lookup, real-data reconciliation, and failure retention. SSP-2.2 — Basic Project State Report Evidence records the report delivery. SSP-2.3 — Project State Interaction Evidence records grouping, search, sorting, clipboard transforms, live behavior, and review evidence. Project State Concept And Architecture owns the resulting reconciliation, report, and lookup contracts.

This delivery builds Project State with the existing local Docs Viewer report-host mechanism plus a versioned Manage-only resolver lookup. It does not introduce generated report Markdown, persist report presentation, or retire the existing image-audit workflow; that belongs to SSP-6 — Project Media Audit Delivery.

Accepted SSP-1 Input

SSP-2 consumes the private dotlineform/projects manage-manifest.json and subject-associations.json as one generation. The Manage manifest supplies subject_generation plus exact document rows whose authoring_subject is {state, kind, key, fields} with optional private evidence. The association product uses docs_subject_associations_v1, repeats that generation and exact collection, and groups each valid {kind, key} to ordered exact document targets and current Manage locations. SSP-2 must require matching receipts before joining document presentation to folder associations.

Only associations whose subject is {kind: "folder", key: "projects/<path>"} and whose exact key matches a scanned real-folder row enter Project State. Valid folder assignments elsewhere under the base root are ordinary non-participants, as are Work, Series, None, malformed, and conflicting subject rows. The Folder icon, Catalogue icon, warning cue, and Info presentation are Manage UI projections rather than Project State inputs. SSP-2 takes subject identity exclusively from normalized state and the matching association receipt.

Complete Outcome

One ordinary human-authored document in scope dotlineform declares viewer_report: project_state and viewer_report_access: local. When the report mounts, it runs a fresh server-side reconciliation and renders a three-column table: Folder, Series, and Docs. Each row originates from one scanned real folder. Project documents join by exact normalized folder_path, while canonical Works join independently through the row key projects/<project_folder>; a document never mediates the Work relationship. The Project State Work projection reads only work_id, project_folder, and series_ids; Studio catalogue/media retains project_subfolder, project_filename, and exact media resolution. The displayed Series cell projects only exact linked Series names and remains blank when none exist. The response retains canonical Work and Series-membership evidence without turning absent or incomplete membership into a browser diagnosis. Project State counts records in works.json; it does not enumerate files or distinguish draft from published Works.

The producer scans the immediate project directories under $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/projects/ only; nested directories remain contents of their owning project row. Every row therefore has an exact normalized key beginning projects/ with one project-directory segment. Report labels remove that guaranteed prefix, so projects/curve poems (2025) appears as curve poems (2025). Finder activation and all lookup joins continue to use the complete normalized key.

Each successful run returns one complete versioned Project State JSON response containing generation/run context and the typed data needed to render and activate every row. The browser holds that response as one ephemeral source; it never joins the authoritative inputs. Folder is the default projection, with one row per real folder. SSP-2.3 adds one bounded icon-pill toggle between Folder and Series: in Folder view the action shows the established list icon and is labelled Group by Series; in Series view it shows a folder icon and is labelled Group by Folder. Series view derives one row per Series-folder relationship from the same response and changes the visible order to Series, Folder, Docs. Dynamic case-insensitive substring search covers the visible text in all three columns after every input change, and every column supports deterministic ascending/descending sorting without another server request.

For example:

Folder Series Docs
curve poems (2025) opens in Finder curve poems one or more exact Project-document links
example/document-only opens in Finder one or more exact Project-document links
example/works-only opens in Finder series 1
example/folder-only opens in Finder

If a folder's Works belong to two Series, the Series cell renders one exact linked name per Series. The response retains the underlying Work identities and membership counts for validation and later purpose-specific consumers, but the displayed report does not present those counts or interpret missing Series membership.

Opening Project State and selecting Run/Refresh perform the same complete server operation: scan, join, validate, return live rows, and atomically publish the matching resolver lookup. A successful refresh replaces the browser row set and reapplies the active search and sort. A failed run shows a contained error rather than an older result; the previous complete resolver lookup remains available and is marked stale. SSP-2 adds no Docs Viewer or Studio mutation hook. SSP-3 owns refreshing the lookup once as a Manage build prerequisite when the selected documents actually require Project Resolver Tokens.

The mounted report offers Copy table and Copy Markdown. Both serialize the current grouping's filtered rows in their current sort order and visible column order. Copy table emits semantic TSV with visible link text for direct spreadsheet paste. Copy Markdown emits the plain-text line Project State - YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, using the report generation time in GMT, then one blank line and a Markdown table retaining exact Folder, Project-document, and Series links. Folder view keeps one physical folder per output row and joins multiple cell values with ; ; Series view intentionally emits one row per Series-folder relationship and repeats folder/Docs context for multi-Series folders. Neither transform performs a network request, persists report state, creates an archive, or shows a success message.

SSP-3 can consume the accepted lookup as soon as its generation, failure, and access contracts are proven. The current /studio/project-state/ route and var/studio/reports/project-state.md remain until SSP-6 preserves and renames their image-audit capability.

Fixed Design Notes

  • The normalized relationship is scanned real folder -> documents[] and, independently, scanned real folder -> works[] -> series memberships[].
  • One scanned real folder is one immediate project directory under $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/projects/; its nested directories remain contents rather than Project State rows.
  • One row represents one real folder established by the current scan. Multiple Project documents, Works, and Series remain ordered arrays rather than duplicate rows or scalar shortcuts.
  • Only documents with one valid folder_path beginning projects/ and exactly matching a scanned row participate. Valid assignments elsewhere under the base root, no-subject, Work-subject, Series-subject, malformed, conflicting, and recorded-only paths remain outside Project State.
  • Every canonical Work projects to projects/<project_folder> for its Project State join. Project State reads only work_id, project_folder, and series_ids; Studio catalogue/media retains project_subfolder, project_filename, exact media resolution, draft/published status, and publication date.
  • Matched Works are grouped by canonical Series ID. Each Series count retained in the response is the number of matched Work records whose series_ids include that ID; one Work may contribute to more than one Series count. Browser presentation uses only exact linked Series names.
  • Folder identity is relative to $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/, while the complete scan boundary is its projects/ subtree. The report displays only the remaining first-level name after omitting projects/; identity and activation retain the complete key.
  • Project State is a local report module mounted by an ordinary stable Docs Viewer document through the existing report registry, allowlisted loader, and report service.
  • Mount and explicit Run/Refresh perform the full scan. Rendered rows are ephemeral browser state; no generated Markdown, persisted presentation snapshot, report-source rewrite, or filesystem watcher is introduced.
  • One complete live JSON response supplies both browser projections. Folder view uses one row per scanned folder; Series view derives one row per Series-folder relationship without changing the response, reconciliation, or resolver lookup.
  • Search is a dynamic case-insensitive substring match over the visible Folder, Series, and Docs text. Every column sorts in both directions with normalized folder identity as the deterministic final tie-break.
  • Copy table emits semantic TSV for Excel. Copy Markdown emits Project State - YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM from the report generation time in GMT, one blank line, then a Markdown table with exact links. Both include the current visible headings and filtered/sorted projection. Folder view retains one folder per row; Series view retains one Series-folder relationship per row and repeats folder/Docs context when required.
  • The folder lookup returns Work[] + Series[] + Project documents[] for one exact folder subject. Work and Series items carry semantic catalogue identity rather than stored titles or URLs; Series membership is retained without Work publication status.
  • Report mount and explicit Run/Refresh are the only SSP-2 operations that publish the lookup. Studio and Docs mutations retain their existing owners and add no Project State observer or synchronization hook.
  • SSP-3 refreshes Project State once before rendering a selected Manage build that contains Project Resolver Tokens. Refresh ordering, token detection, generation agreement, and failure presentation belong to that consumer delivery rather than SSP-2 mutation paths.
  • A failed write-enabled Project State run never rolls back or repeats a Work or document mutation. The prior complete lookup is retained and marked stale.
  • Project State is Manage-only derived data and unusable as canonical truth.

Delivery Discipline

SSP-2 is inherently larger than the completed Projects glue deliveries, so its size is controlled per checkpoint rather than hidden in one replacement diff. It composes existing canonical readers, the Projects Manage manifest, exact Docs Viewer report seams, and generated-payload writers around one Project-specific producer.

SSP-2.0 was a short scope-and-spec sanity gate over the live producer/lookup and existing report-host fit. The later closeout decision removed the tentative targeted follow-through because the report is already self-refreshing and the only planned lookup consumer can refresh immediately before use. A new reporting framework, generic graph, event bus, repair system, rewritten catalogue reader, or media-audit migration remains scope creep.

SSP-2.2 intentionally stops with an independently useful Folder-first basic report whose data, links, states, and layout can be accepted before browser refinements. SSP-2.3 adds the bounded Folder/Series grouping control, search, sorting, and both clipboard formats over that accepted live response without changing the server reconciliation or resolver lookup. SSP-3 need not wait for those presentation refinements once the lookup's generation, failure, and access contracts are accepted.

Delivery Steps

SSP-2.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [x] Sanity-check the folder-centred Project State, Series-grouped canonical Work counts, live report, focused lookup, and tentative targeted-follow-through outcome against the accepted SSP-1 Projects subject contract, current catalogue, Projects manifest, existing local report modules, report service, and post-commit models; resolve only contradictions that would change the result. The closeout decision below later retires that tentative follow-through.
  • [x] Time the bounded real scan and confirm automatic run-on-mount is suitable; stop for review if observed behavior requires a different mount decision.
  • [x] Confirm the broad blast radius across folder inventory/reconciliation, canonical Works and Series reads, Project associations, versioned lookup, report registry/loader/service, live Run/Refresh, and tentative post-commit impact handling later retired at closeout.
  • [x] Confirm the deliverables: one ordinary local report host, one complete live Folder/Series/Docs JSON response, Folder-first and Series-first browser projections, all-column dynamic search, deterministic column sorting, TSV and Markdown clipboard transforms, exact scanned-folder lookup, automatic mount run, explicit refresh, lookup stale-state retention, focused evidence, concise durable owner updates, and the tentative bounded follow-through later retired at closeout.
  • [x] Stop for review if the result requires a new report mechanism, generic graph, event bus, repair system, rewritten catalogue reader, media-audit migration, report-result cache, or another boundary excluded above. Do not produce an exact file inventory, line estimate, frozen implementation, fixture implementation, or complete test architecture at this gate.

Checkpoint: SSP-2.0 — Project State Sanity Note confirms the revised typed-subject spec, scheduling dependencies, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, local/public boundary, and stop condition. SSP-2.1 implementation was approved after this checkpoint.

SSP-2.1 — Build The Folder-Centred Producer And Lookup

  • [x] Implement the confined immediate-child scan of $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/projects/ that establishes the complete project-folder row inventory before recorded-system evidence is joined; prove nested directories, the base root, and sibling trees remain with their current owners rather than becoming rows.
  • [x] Build one exact Project-document index from the customisation-owned Manage manifest and one independent canonical Work index keyed as projects/<normalized project_folder>; read only work_id, project_folder, and series_ids for that Work projection, and left-join both indexes to scanned rows without allowing either recorded route to create a row.
  • [x] Retain each matched canonical Work by semantic identity and current canonical series_ids.
  • [x] Derive each folder's ordered Series memberships and exact Work counts from the retained Works' canonical series_ids.
  • [x] Retain fully reconciled, document-only, Works-only, folder-only, duplicate-document, and incomplete-Series states for scanned rows without treating other authoring-subject kinds or recorded-only paths as Project State rows.
  • [x] Return one validated versioned live report JSON envelope with generation/run context, complete typed rows, exact presentation/link targets, and a distinct matched-Work count suitable for deterministic sorting; atomically publish the matching versioned scanned-folder-keyed lookup whose groups are Work[] + Series[] + Project documents[].
  • [x] Prove lookup rows contain semantic Work/Series identities and exact Series membership without Work publication status, Work/Series document associations, stored catalogue URLs, or live-scan fallbacks.

Checkpoint: SSP-2.1 — Project State Producer Evidence records passing physical-inventory, independent document/Work join, normalization, Series-membership-count, lookup-schema, generation, failure-retention, and public-isolation evidence. The independent code/diff review confirms the physical scan alone establishes rows, the producer retains exact Work identity while catalogue presentation keeps its existing owner, and recorded-only paths retain a separate report owner. SSP-2 is stopped before SSP-2.2 implementation approval.

SSP-2.2 — Deliver The Basic Docs Viewer Report

  • [x] Create one ordinary human-authored report-host document in scope dotlineform with viewer_report: project_state, viewer_report_access: local, concise explanatory Markdown, and ordinary Docs Viewer reachability.
  • [x] Register and allowlist one focused project_state module through the existing report registry, loader, management report service, and local access boundary.
  • [x] Run the report automatically on mount, provide explicit Run/Refresh, and render the live Folder/Series/Docs table with compact run context, Finder-opening folder names without secondary state labels, exact linked Series names, blank Series/Docs cells for absent values, and exact Project-document links.
  • [x] Apply the display-only folder rule: projects/<path> appears as <path>, while stored identity, lookup joins, producer reconciliation state, and dlf-local: activation retain the complete base-relative key.
  • [x] On failure, render a contained current-run error without older rows while retaining and marking the previous complete lookup stale.
  • [x] Verify automatic mount, explicit refresh, service/report agreement, busy/error/empty states, long cells, exact links, and basic table presentation at representative laptop/desktop widths.

Checkpoint: SSP-2.2 — Basic Project State Report Evidence records the ordinary report host, local registry/loader/service boundary, automatic run, explicit refresh, generation agreement, current-run failure clearing, exact links, and representative Folder-first presentation evidence. The independent code/diff review confirms the accepted report is independently usable and the existing reporting mechanism remains its sole owner. Alternate grouping, search, sorting, and clipboard refinements remain SSP-2.3-owned; mutation follow-through remained tentative until the closeout decision below retired it; Studio media-audit retirement remains SSP-6-owned.

SSP-2.3 — Add Report Grouping, Search, Sorting, And Copy

  • [x] Use the accepted live response as one ephemeral browser row set without changing the SSP-2.1 response schema, server reconciliation, or resolver lookup.
  • [x] Add one bounded icon-pill toggle whose icon, tooltip, and accessible label name the destination action: list / Group by Series from Folder view, and folder / Group by Folder from Series view. Folder is the initial projection with columns Folder, Series, Docs and one row per scanned folder. Series uses columns Series, Folder, Docs and derives one row per exact Series-folder relationship, repeating the folder and its Docs for each Series membership.
  • [x] Keep every scanned folder visible in Series view. A folder without an exact Series route retains one row with a blank Series cell; do not add a diagnostic label, hide the folder, or create a Series-keyed server product.
  • [x] Implement dynamic case-insensitive substring search over the visible Folder, Series, and Docs text after every input change, with no network request or hidden-identity matching.
  • [x] Add ascending/descending sorting to every visible column using its current projection values and normalized folder identity as the final deterministic tie-break. Each projection starts with its leading column ascending; switching projection preserves search and selects that leading sort; successful refresh preserves grouping and reapplies active search and sort.
  • [x] Add the established Copy Table icon pill as a semantic TSV transform of the current filtered/sorted projection and an MD pill as a Markdown transform of that same projection; retain Copy table and Copy Markdown as their accessible labels and tooltips. Copy Markdown starts with Project State - YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM using the response's report generation time converted to GMT, follows it with one blank line, and then emits the table. Include the visible headings and order, retain exact Markdown links, and use visible link text in TSV. Folder view keeps one folder per row and joins multiple cell entries with ; ; Series view keeps one Series-folder relationship per row and may repeat folder/Docs context. Avoid server requests, automatic document creation, saved exports, and persisted report state, and show no success message.
  • [x] Verify both projections with fixtures and the observed live multi-Series folders, including exact Series routes without displayed Work counts, repeated Series-view folder/Docs context, blank Series/Docs values, search and sort composition, refresh-state reapplication, pure TSV output, the exact GMT Markdown preamble and blank line, Markdown-table serialization, and the absence of interaction-time requests. Keep exact live paths in delivery evidence rather than the durable contract; keep durable automated coverage at the pure data/projection boundary and manually check grouping, clipboard, and visual interaction behavior.

Checkpoint: SSP-2.3 — Project State Interaction Evidence records passing focused Folder/Series projection, multi-Series live-data, unmatched-state, all-column search, deterministic sorting, refresh-state, TSV, Markdown, and local-only evidence. The independent code/diff review confirms the refinements consume only the accepted in-memory response, preserve each projection's declared row grain, and leave the server and resolver contracts unchanged.

SSP-2.4 — Close Out And Transfer Lookup Freshness

  • [x] Confirm the shipped report already refreshes the complete live response and atomically replaces the versioned lookup on mount and explicit Run/Refresh.
  • [x] Remove the tentative Studio and Docs post-commit impact classifiers, targeted row updates, and synchronization hooks from SSP-2; they add no value to the independently useful report and are premature without a lookup consumer.
  • [x] Transfer consumption-time freshness to SSP-3: a selected Manage build containing Project Resolver Tokens refreshes Project State once after current subject products are available and before token rendering, never once per token.
  • [x] Retain explicit generation agreement, stale/unavailable failure presentation, source stability, and public isolation as SSP-3 acceptance evidence without making canonical mutations depend on the derived lookup.
  • [x] Reconcile the delivery, Project State architecture, Resolver Tokens architecture/delivery, and Sub-Scope Publishing owner; retain SSP-6 ownership of the existing Studio image audit.

Checkpoint: SSP-2 closes without additional production code after SSP-2.3. The report and its producer remain independently useful, the persisted lookup remains the atomic Project State product, and SSP-3 owns refreshing that product immediately before a relevant Manage build consumes it. No Studio or Docs mutation hook is introduced.

Not In Scope

  • automatic repair or synchronization;
  • mutation controls in the report;
  • image discovery or primary-image auditing, which belongs to SSP-6;
  • a detail-level report whose rows or grouping follow project_subfolder, which would be a separate future report and delivery;
  • scanning $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/ itself or reporting physical folders and recorded paths outside its projects/ subtree;
  • reverse reconciliation of document or Work paths that do not match a scanned real folder, which belongs to a separate report;
  • continuous folder watching;
  • Studio or Docs post-commit Project State synchronization hooks;
  • downloaded CSV/TSV files, saved export history, or automatic clipboard persistence;
  • arbitrary column layouts, user-authored grouping definitions, or a second Series-keyed server response;
  • public Project State data;
  • Work/Series reverse associations, Manage index subject cues, editorial copy, or public Work/Series doc_url[] projection;
  • retirement of /studio/project-state/ or var/studio/reports/project-state.md, which belongs to SSP-6; or
  • Resolver Token parsing and rendering, which belongs to SSP-3.

Completion Evidence

  • Fixture and real-data evidence prove the physical scan alone establishes folder rows and independent joins produce fully reconciled, document-only, Works-only, folder-only, duplicate-document, and incomplete-Series states.
  • The ordinary report host automatically runs and renders the Folder-first Folder/Series/Docs response, presents only the first-level folder name without a prefix or secondary state label, and offers explicit Run/Refresh.
  • The browser derives the Series-first Series/Folder/Docs projection from the same response, repeats multi-Series folder/Docs context once per Series, and retains every scanned folder with blank Series values where no exact Series route exists.
  • Both projections search visible text across all columns after each input change, sort every column deterministically, and reapply grouping/search/sort state after refresh without joining inputs or making interaction-time requests.
  • Copy table produces pure semantic TSV suitable for Excel. Copy Markdown produces the exact GMT generation-time preamble, one blank line, and a linked Markdown table from the current projection, preserving its visible column order and row grain without persisted report state or automatic archival.
  • Each full run observes direct Finder changes, returns current rows, and publishes one matching resolver-lookup generation without persisting report presentation.
  • Producer tests show relationship-generation changes for exact scanned-folder matches, no Project State row creation from recorded-only paths, and no report-generation effect from Work subfolder, filename, title, status, or publication-date changes.
  • Real-data evidence retains Works whose images live below a project_subfolder on the first-level project_folder row and counts them through their current series_ids.
  • SSP-3 receives one current lookup generation from its relevant-build prerequisite, then resolves one folder row to semantic Work/Series descriptors and exact Project-document targets without scanning during token expansion.
  • Public projections contain no local folder paths, Project State data, lookup path, service URL, or refresh capability.
  • The current Studio image-audit workflow remains unchanged for SSP-6 rather than being partially retired here.
